notice: General guidance for US nonprofits, not legal advice. Review with your counsel or accountant; rules differ by country, state and type of organization.

obligations.name: Corporate or state annual report
obligations.instructions: Most US states ask nonprofit corporations to file an annual or biennial report with the Secretary of State (or the state's corporations division) to stay in good standing: usually the officers and directors, the registered agent and the principal address, sometimes with a small fee. Look up your state's due date (often the anniversary month of incorporation or a fixed date), set it as the Next Due Date, and set Recurrence to Every Two Years if your state asks for a biennial report. Add one obligation for each other state where you are registered to do business. General guidance, not legal advice: review with your counsel.

obligations.name: Annual tax return (US: IRS Form 990 series)
obligations.instructions: US tax-exempt organizations file one return of the Form 990 series each year, which one depending on size and type: Form 990-N (e-Postcard) for small organizations, Form 990-EZ, Form 990, or Form 990-PF for private foundations. It is generally due by the 15th day of the 5th month after your fiscal year ends (15 May for a calendar year), and Form 8868 gives an automatic extension. An organization that does not file for three consecutive years loses its exemption automatically. Many states also ask for a copy or their own annual charity report. Outside the US, rename this obligation and its instructions for your country's equivalent. General guidance, not legal advice: confirm with your accountant.

obligations.name: Charitable solicitation registration
obligations.jurisdiction: Each state where you ask for donations
obligations.instructions: Many US states ask a charity to register before it asks their residents for donations, and to renew each year, often with financial statements and a fee. Some states exempt small or religious organizations. Copy this obligation for each state where you solicit, with that state in Jurisdiction and its renewal date as the Next Due Date. General guidance, not legal advice: review with your counsel.

obligations.name: Insurance renewals
obligations.instructions: Review and renew the organization's insurance before each policy ends: commonly general liability, directors and officers (D and O), property, workers' compensation where you have employees, and any coverage a funder, landlord or partner requires. Keep each policy's declarations page in this obligation's completed cycles, or record each policy as an Agreement of type Insurance Policy. General guidance, not legal advice.

obligations.name: Annual financial audit or review
obligations.instructions: An independent audit or review of the year's financial statements, when your state's charity registration, a funder or your bylaws ask for one, often above a revenue threshold. Organizations spending a large amount of US federal awards in a year may need a Single Audit. Set the Next Due Date from the deadline that applies to you and keep the final report as evidence. General guidance, not legal advice: confirm with your accountant.

obligations.name: Registered agent renewal
obligations.instructions: Each state where the organization is incorporated or registered needs a registered agent with an address in that state to receive legal papers. If you pay a registered agent service, renew it before it ends; if the agent or address changes, file the change with the state. General guidance, not legal advice.

obligations.name: Record of processing review
obligations.jurisdiction: Where the GDPR or a similar law applies (EU, EEA, UK)
obligations.instructions: The GDPR asks an organization to keep a record of its processing activities: why it holds personal data, about whom, on what lawful basis, who receives it, where it goes and how long it is kept. Keep one Processing Activity per purpose on the Processing Activities tab (starter rows arrive as Draft). Once a year, and whenever you start something new, check each one, set it Active or Retired and complete this cycle. Turn this obligation on only if the GDPR or a similar law applies to you. General guidance, not legal advice: review with your counsel or data protection officer.

obligations.name: Data protection impact assessment (DPIA) reviews
obligations.jurisdiction: Where the GDPR or a similar law applies (EU, EEA, UK)
obligations.instructions: Processing that is likely to be high risk to people (large amounts of special category data, monitoring, new technology) needs a DPIA before it starts, kept up to date. Check DPIA Required on those Processing Activities, keep the assessment as a file on the record and set Next DPIA Review: the owner is reminded before it. Use this obligation for the yearly look across all of them. General guidance, not legal advice: review with your counsel or data protection officer.

policies.name: Conflict of interest policy
policies.summary: Starter record: attach your own policy. A conflict of interest policy usually says what a conflict is, how directors, officers and key staff disclose one (often in a yearly statement), how the board decides on a matter where someone has a conflict, and how that is recorded in the minutes. IRS Form 990, Part VI, asks whether the organization has one and how it is monitored. BarnCRM supplies no legal text. Not legal advice: review your policy with your counsel.

policies.name: Whistleblower policy
policies.summary: Starter record: attach your own policy. A whistleblower policy usually says how staff, volunteers and directors can report suspected wrongdoing, who receives reports, how the reporter is protected from retaliation and how reports are investigated. IRS Form 990, Part VI, asks whether the organization has one. BarnCRM supplies no legal text. Not legal advice: review your policy with your counsel.

policies.name: Document retention and destruction policy
policies.summary: Starter record: attach your own policy. A document retention and destruction policy usually lists kinds of records (governing documents, minutes, tax returns, financial and personnel records, donor records) with how long each is kept, how records are destroyed, and how destruction stops when legal action is expected. IRS Form 990, Part VI, asks whether the organization has one. BarnCRM supplies no legal text. Not legal advice: review your policy with your counsel.

policies.name: Gift acceptance policy
policies.summary: Starter record: attach your own policy. A gift acceptance policy usually says which gifts the organization accepts, which need review before they are accepted (real estate, securities, vehicles, restricted or named gifts), who decides, and how gifts are acknowledged. IRS Form 990, Schedule M, asks about a policy for non-standard contributions. BarnCRM supplies no legal text. Not legal advice: review your policy with your counsel.

policies.name: Data protection policy
policies.summary: Starter record: attach your own policy. A data protection policy usually says what personal data the organization holds and why, who is responsible (and any data protection officer), how staff and volunteers keep data safe, how long it is kept, and how people use their rights. BarnCRM supplies no legal text. Not legal advice: review your policy with your counsel or data protection officer.

policies.name: Privacy notice
policies.summary: Starter record: attach your own notice. A privacy notice tells donors, volunteers, participants and others what data you collect, why and on what lawful basis, who receives it, how long you keep it and how to use their rights or complain. Keep it in step with your record of processing. BarnCRM supplies no legal text. Not legal advice: review your notice with your counsel.

policies.name: Data subject request procedure
policies.summary: Starter record: attach your own procedure. It usually says how a request is recognized and logged (a Data Subject Request record), how identity is checked, who answers and by when (one month under the GDPR), and how an erasure is done (Erase Person on the person, with the request number as the reference). BarnCRM supplies no legal text. Not legal advice: review with your counsel.

policies.name: Personal data breach response procedure
policies.summary: Starter record: attach your own procedure. It usually says how staff and volunteers report a suspected breach at once, who assesses the risk, how it is contained, when the supervisory authority is told (within 72 hours under the GDPR, unless it is unlikely to result in a risk) and when the people affected are told. Log every breach as a Data Breach record, reported or not. BarnCRM supplies no legal text. Not legal advice: review with your counsel.

processingActivities.name: Donor records and fundraising
processingActivities.purpose: Recording gifts and pledges, thanking and receipting donors, and asking for further support.
processingActivities.dataCategories: Name, contact details, gift history, communication preferences, notes from contact.
processingActivities.recipients: Your payment processor, email service and mailing house, where you use them.
processingActivities.retention: Set your own, for example gifts kept for the years tax law asks.

processingActivities.name: Email newsletter
processingActivities.purpose: Sending news and appeals by email to people who asked for them.
processingActivities.dataCategories: Name, email address, sign-up date and source, opt-out.
processingActivities.retention: Until the person unsubscribes, plus a suppression record.

processingActivities.name: Volunteer management
processingActivities.purpose: Recruiting, scheduling and thanking volunteers, and recording their hours and checks.
processingActivities.dataCategories: Name, contact details, availability, skills, hours, onboarding and check results.
processingActivities.retention: Set your own, for example for a set time after the last shift.

processingActivities.name: Program participants
processingActivities.purpose: Delivering services and recording enrollments, attendance and outcomes.
processingActivities.dataCategories: Name, contact details, enrollment and attendance, case notes; may include special category data such as health.
processingActivities.recipients: Funders receive totals only, unless you agree otherwise.
processingActivities.retention: Set your own, often tied to funder or legal requirements.

processingActivities.name: Staff and board records
processingActivities.purpose: Employing staff and running the board.
processingActivities.dataCategories: Name, contact details, role, terms, conflict-of-interest disclosures.
processingActivities.recipients: Payroll provider, pension provider, authorities as the law requires.
processingActivities.retention: Set your own, as employment and tax law ask.

assessments.title: Board Self-Assessment
questions: The board understands the organization's mission and uses it to guide decisions.
The board reviews the organization's finances regularly and understands them.
Board members receive the packet early enough to prepare for meetings.
Meetings focus on strategy and decisions rather than reports.
Every member takes part in discussion, and differing views are welcome.
The board's committees have clear charges and report back on them.
The board oversees the executive director's performance and pay each year.
Members understand their legal duties of care, loyalty and obedience.
Conflicts of interest are disclosed and handled as the policy requires.
The board has the skills, experience and diversity of views it needs.
New members receive an orientation that prepares them to contribute.
Every member supports fundraising in a way that suits them.
I am satisfied with my own contribution to the board this year.
